quantifiers: For every probability space (Omega,mu), every jointly measurable symmetric nonnegative kernel W for which the displayed integral operator is bounded L-infinity to L-one, and every bounded measurable test pair u,v

trusted_foundation.statement: If W is nonnegative almost everywhere and f is nonnegative almost everywhere, then the Lebesgue integral defining A_W f is nonnegative almost everywhere.
trusted_foundation.source: Standard: monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral

trusted_foundation.statement: For bounded u,v, the pairing integral u(x)W(x,y)v(y)dmu(x)dmu(y) is integrable and Fubini identifies it with both iterated forms.
trusted_foundation.source: Bogachev, Measure Theory: Fubini theorem for integrable functions

trusted_foundation.statement: Swap x and y in the product integral and use W(x,y)=W(y,x) almost everywhere to obtain <u,A_W v>=<v,A_W u> for every bounded u,v.
trusted_foundation.source: Standard: product-measure coordinate swap and equality almost everywhere

trusted_foundation.statement: A graphop is a bounded L-infinity to L-one P-operator that is positivity preserving and self-adjoint under the displayed bilinear pairing.
trusted_foundation.source: Definition in arXiv:2602.08785v1, Definition 3.1, anchor S3.Thmtheorem1

limitations: The certificate exposes Fubini and integral monotonicity as its standard measure-theory trust boundary. It does not reduce Lebesgue integration to set theory.
